investigations.name: as-forage-and-survival
investigations.title: Forage Both & Outlive a Non-Mover
investigations.objective: Does the evolved forager keep both nutrients alive by visiting both resources, and does it survive longer than a passive agent?
investigations.claim: The agent forages both resources in 12 of 16 FAR, high-drain environments (sep 42-62, asymmetric per-nutrient drain) and is STATE-DEPENDENT: it uses its internal nutrient sensors to prioritize the faster-draining resource (ablating them costs +226 survival + 2 forages-both), rather than the blind circling of the earlier regime.

investigations.name: as-morphology-comparison
investigations.title: Three Morphologies' Sensing
investigations.objective: How do the three morphologies differ in what they can sense, and which is the agent analyzed here?
investigations.claim: The three morphologies differ in chemosensor placement and whether they have internal nutrient sensors; the evolved, analyzed agent is morphology M2 (one front stalk + nutrient sensors).

investigations.name: as-switching-dynamics
investigations.title: The Dynamical Signature of Switching
investigations.objective: What is the dynamical signature of the agent's action switching — how do its distance-to-resource and internal nutrient states evolve as it alternates?
investigations.claim: Distance to A and B are anti-phase and the nutrients sawtooth in step with engagement — the agent rhythmically switches between foraging the two resources.

investigations.name: cat-catch-and-avoid
investigations.description:
The seeded CTRNN agent (5 neurons, 7 ray sensors, 2 motors) is decoded from
data/genomes/categorical_perception.npz and run deterministically. The
behaviour is pinned by tests/test_categorical_seed.py.
investigations.title: Catch Circles, Avoid Diamonds
investigations.objective:
Does the evolved agent catch falling circles and avoid falling diamonds from
the committed seeded genome, across the trained range of object offsets?
investigations.claim:
The agent catches circles (mean final distance 0.15, caught at all offsets) and
avoids diamonds (mean final distance 29.6) — a category gap > 8.

investigations.name: cat-categorization-map
investigations.description:
The committed seed is replayed over 33 offsets in [−8, 8] for each shape. The
map is the signature categorization plot of Beer (2003).
investigations.title: Categorization Map & Generalization Edge
investigations.objective:
How does the agent's final distance to the object vary with the object's
horizontal offset, for circles vs diamonds — and does the categorization hold
beyond the trained offset range?
investigations.claim:
Circles and diamonds form two separated bands across −8..+6 (catch vs avoid);
the separation collapses at offset ≥7 (untrained), an honest generalization edge.

investigations.name: cat-decision-dynamics
investigations.description:
The committed seed is run at offset +3 for a circle and a diamond; per-step
neuron outputs are recorded and plotted. This connects the behaviour to Beer's
dynamical reading of the decision.
investigations.title: Decision Dynamics (Catch vs Avoid)
investigations.objective:
How do the CTRNN's internal dynamics differ when the agent commits to catching
a circle versus avoiding a diamond presented at the same offset?
investigations.claim:
The coupled neural dynamics commit differently to the two categories: outputs
and the motor-neuron phase trajectory diverge after a shared initial phase.

investigations.name: param-space-codim1-bifurcations
investigations.description:
Built on `analysis.bifurcation_sweep` over a self-weight grid, with
`viz.bifurcation_diagram` colouring branches by stability. The 1→3 transition
is pinned in the test suite (1 equilibrium at w=1.0, 3 at w=8.0).
investigations.title: Codim-1 Pitchfork: 1→3 Equilibria (Beer 2006)
investigations.objective:
As the self-weight of a single center-crossing CTRNN neuron increases, how does
its equilibrium set change, and at what point does bistability appear?
investigations.claim:
On the center-crossing (symmetric, θ=−w/2) slice, a single neuron undergoes a
pitchfork bifurcation at w≈4 from 1 to 3 equilibria as self-weight grows,
reproducing Beer (2006). Off this slice the pitchfork unfolds into saddle-node
folds (see the codim-2 study).

investigations.name: param-space-codim2-structure
investigations.description:
`param_space.codim2_equilibria_count` evaluates the equilibrium count over the
(w, θ) grid; the gallery renders it as a heatmap. A bistable (3-equilibria)
region is present and connected, bounded by two saddle-node fold curves meeting at a cusp (the center-crossing
pitchfork is its symmetric axis); cells exactly on the
fold can register 2 equilibria.
investigations.title: Codim-2 Bistability Wedge (Beer 2022)
investigations.objective:
How is the single-neuron 1→3 transition organised (saddle-node fold curves and a cusp) when both the self-weight
and the bias vary — what is the shape of the bistable region in the
(self-weight, bias) plane?
investigations.claim:
Bistability occupies a connected cusp wedge in (self-weight, bias), reproducing
the codim-2 structure of Beer (2022).

investigations.name: param-space-equilibria-and-nullclines
investigations.description:
Using the workspace's `analysis` layer (nullcline grid, multi-start equilibria,
Jacobian eigenvalues) and `viz.phase_portrait_2d`, we render the phase portrait
and read off the geometry. The sustained-oscillation behaviour is also pinned
by the CTRNN test suite (tail output range well above a settle threshold).
investigations.title: Equilibria, Nullclines & Oscillation (2-neuron)
investigations.objective:
What is the phase-plane geometry of a two-neuron center-crossing CTRNN with
mixed-sign reciprocal coupling — where are its nullclines and equilibrium, and
is that equilibrium stable or does the circuit oscillate?
investigations.claim:
The 2-neuron center-crossing circuit has a single unstable interior
equilibrium and oscillates — a minimal central pattern generator.

investigations.name: cpg-limit-cycle
investigations.title: The CPG's Limit Cycle
investigations.objective:
Is the walking rhythm a dynamical attractor of the CTRNN — does the network's
state trace a stable closed loop (a limit cycle), the signature of a central
pattern generator?
investigations.claim:
The evolved CTRNN's state traces a clean closed loop in its activity space — a
limit cycle — repeating once per stride (~19.8 steps). The rhythm is a
self-sustaining attractor, not a clocked or scripted sequence.

investigations.name: gait-and-velocity
investigations.title: Gait Quantified — Stride, Duty, Velocity
investigations.objective:
What gait does the evolved walker produce — how regular is its stride, how is
stance/swing balanced, and how fast does the body move?
investigations.claim:
A regular gait: stride period 19.8 ± 0.4 steps (the spread is only ~2% of the
period), duty factor 0.44 (stance and swing nearly balanced), mean body
velocity ~9.0 units/time (~0.9 units/step).

investigations.name: walk-forward
investigations.title: The Walker Walks Forward
investigations.objective:
Does the evolved CTRNN drive the leg so the body travels steadily forward,
with a repeating step cycle rather than a single lunge?
investigations.claim:
The evolved walker travels ~450 units over a 500-step trial and never
reverses, taking 25 regular steps — a sustained forward walk, not a one-off
lunge (which a pure-distance fitness produces, reaching only ~21).

investigations.name: memory-dynamics
investigations.title: Object 1 Held in Memory
investigations.objective:
Is the first object's size actually held in the CTRNN's state across the
inter-stimulus interval, when no object is present — i.e. is this real memory?
investigations.claim:
Yes. During the ISI (object absent), the agent's neural state encodes object
1's size with correlation 0.88: the trace is set while object 1 falls and
persists through the blank interval until object 2 arrives. Memory realized as
CTRNN dynamics, not a stored value.

investigations.name: relative-size-discrimination
investigations.title: Catch the Larger, Avoid the Smaller
investigations.objective:
Does the evolved agent catch the second object when it is larger than the
first and avoid it when smaller — above what any memoryless policy can do?
investigations.claim:
The agent categorizes by RELATIVE size, reaching 0.688 accuracy (catch 0.625,
avoid 0.75) — above the 0.625 ceiling that any single-object (memoryless)
policy can reach on this role-balanced battery, and above the 0.5 always-catch
/ always-avoid baselines.
